text:
leo park: Heads-up: onboarding v5-int4 tonight. QA shows many tiny per-slice drops (~0.3-1%) spread across business and longform slices. Individually below alarms but dashboard aggregate looks worrying. Thinking we should record a formal "regret ledger" + automated gating rules instead of only per-slice hard cutoffs. Thoughts?

anya smirnov: define regret ledger? sounds close to cumulative delta but with bookkeeping?

leo park: yes. ledger tracks positive regressions over time per-slice and per-metric, with decay and an adjustable budget. Actions fire at budget bands (notify, shift-percent-to-fallback, full rollback). Ledger also records converted credits from latency or cost wins.

jess ramos: I like ledger for auditability. We can snapshot ledger entries into rollout history for postmortem. Also add a per-slice "importance" multiplier (e.g., billing-critical slices) so tiny drops on high-value slices matter more.

omar el-amin: ops question: what metrics are in ledger? mrr, correctness, hallucination rate?

leo park: multi-metric by default: regret = sum_k weight_k * max(0, baseline_k - variant_k). Default weights: mrr=1.0, rouge_f1=0.5, halluc_rate=2.0 (tunable). We store weights in model-registry and expose them to rollout service.

anya smirnov: add cap on per-slice contribution so one bad small slice can't empty the budget. cap=3% by default. Also require p90/p95 quantiles for stability instead of raw means.

jess ramos: for action semantics propose progressive steps: 1) warn channel + dashboard card; 2) shift 25% traffic to fallback for N minutes; 3) shift 75%; 4) full rollback. Each step requires observation window and minimum time between steps to avoid oscillation.

leo park: minimal pseudo-config (single-line JSON style in thread): {"policy":"ledger-budget","capacity":0.06,"decay_per_min":0.0012,"slice_weight":"traffic*importance","per_slice_cap":0.03,"metric_weights":"mrr:1,rouge:0.5,halo:2","quantile":95,"bands":"warn:0.6,step1:0.8,step2:0.9,rollback:0.98","partial_steps":"0.25,0.75","step_window_min":10,"cooldown_min":30}

omar el-amin: can routing expose slice traffic and importance fast enough? @infra-bot

infra-bot: metrics: per-slice traffic and deltas available via /metrics/slices every 60s. Can enable 15s export for rollout watchers if requested. Importance factors are read from model-registry API.

anya smirnov: nice. Two extra asks: 1) convert latency gains to ledger credit with a tunable factor; 2) store full contributor list on triggers for root-cause.

jess ramos: agree. Also add manual override flag at rollout UI and a "sales-day" mode to increase budget temporarily.

leo park: simulation plan: run historical backtest over last 60 days with capacity 6% and decay 0.072/hr to estimate false-positive rate and time-in-partial. I'll run sim tonight.

omar el-amin: logging: emit signed_ledger (positive = regret, negative = credit), absolute_ledger, top5 slice contributors, and config_hash on every action. Keep time series for 30 days.

anya smirnov: I'll update model-registry schema: fields policy_name, policy_config_blob_url, expected_fpr, metric_weights_url. Also add UI link to sim results.

infra-bot: deploy-bot: scheduled canary for v5-int4 start=1755560000. Health checks: p95 latency, error-rate, ledger-budget. Partial fallback path enabled.

leo park: thanks. If sim looks good I'll submit PR with unit tests and a small canary flag to enable ledger-policy. Ping me on results. :eyes:

jess ramos: one more thing  include a small A/B shadow (quiet burn) for 10% traffic before enabling full canary so we get an early ledger signal without affecting latency-sensitive routes.

leo park: good call. will add shadow traffic step. moving to action items. :rocket:
